questions.question: When are events $A$ and $B$ conditionally independent given $C$?
questions.explanation: $A$ and $B$ are conditionally independent given $C$ when $P(A\cap B\mid C)=P(A\mid C)P(B\mid C)$ (the factorization holds within $C$).
questions.source_support: The definition states $P(A\cap B\mid C)=P(A\mid C)P(B\mid C)$.

option_explanations: $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$ is ordinary (unconditional) independence, not conditional independence given $C$.
$A\cap B=\emptyset$ is disjointness, not conditional independence.
$P(C)=0$ makes conditioning on $C$ undefined, not conditionally independent.
